sections.h2: Henry County offices and phone numbers
sections.html:
Both property tax offices are at 100 West Franklin in Clinton, ZIP 64735. The assessor can be reached at 660-885-7212 and keeps early hours, 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday to Friday, with weekend or evening visits by appointment. A GIS mapping link sits on the assessor's page.

Bills come from a different desk. The Henry County Treasurer serves as Ex Officio Collector of Revenue, at 660-885-7207, fax 660-885-7259, collector@henrycountymo.net. Value questions go to the assessor. Balance questions go to the collector.

Henry County is in west-central Missouri, with Clinton as the seat and largest town. The population estimate is 22,671 and the county has 10,750 housing units, 75.0 percent of them owner-occupied. A typical owned home is valued at $160,600. Owning costs $1,212 a month with a mortgage, median gross rent is $768, and median household income is $57,926. Only 18 building permits were issued in 2025, so resale drives most of the market.

Much of the county is hilly and wooded ground next to the Truman Reservoir, and hunting and fishing draw buyers. A parcel with shoreline, timber or creek frontage will be marketed differently from a town lot in Clinton or Windsor, and its assessment class can differ too, because farm and residential ground carry different rates.

Buyers often ask which school district a house is in, and the assessor's parcel record answers that.

The assessor taxes a fixed share of market value: 19 percent for homes, 12 percent for farmland and 32 percent for commercial property, as RSMo 137.115 provides. New values go on the books in odd-numbered years and carry through the even year after.

  • A home value that climbs more than 15 percent, apart from new construction, calls for an on-site inspection.
  • The owner is told in writing and has at least 30 days to ask for a look inside.
  • A drive-by does not meet the statute.

If a jump like that is appealed, RSMo 138.060 puts the burden on the assessor to show the value is no higher than market value.

Start with the county Board of Equalization, whose filing cutoff is the second Monday in July. If the Board rules against you, the State Tax Commission allows 30 days from the date of the Board's letter. You can file online, by email to Legal@stc.mo.gov or by mail to PO Box 146, Jefferson City, MO 65102-0146.

Property held by a company, trust or estate needs a lawyer to file. Attach the tax bill or the Board's letter to your complaint and nothing more at first. Signing an agreed value with the assessor ends your right to appeal further. Phone 660-885-7212 for the local forms.

Missouri taxes whoever holds the property on January 1, so timing around that date matters to a seller.

Henry County property tax dates
WhenWhat happens
January 1Assessment date
Odd yearsNew real estate values
Second Monday in JulyBoard of Equalization filing cutoff
December 31Bill due; mailed payments judged by postmark under RSMo 139.100
After January 1Collector adds penalty
Fourth Monday in AugustSale of delinquent land

Call the collector for this year's mailing date and the penalty figure.

The county may sell delinquent land on the fourth Monday of August. RSMo 140.150 lets the owner stop the sale by paying tax, penalty, interest and costs to the collector first. Notice goes by first class mail to the recorded owner, and a letter that never shows up cancels nothing.

Request a payoff from 660-885-7207 before you list and give the figure to your title company. If you dispute the value, RSMo 139.031 permits payment under protest: pay in full before delinquency, send the collector a written statement and file a circuit court suit within ninety days.

A house with unpaid years, an inherited title or tenants in place can still sell. A cash buyer does not need a lender's appraisal, and the tax payoff comes out of your proceeds at closing, so the sale does not stall on a county balance.

sections.h2: What to gather before you list
sections.html:
Pull the parcel record from the assessor, including the school district, and ask the collector for the current balance. Together they tell a buyer what the land is classed as, what the bill is and whether anything is overdue.

If your value jumped, note the date on the notice. The Board of Equalization window runs only until the second Monday in July, and an agreed value signed with the assessor closes the door on further appeals. When timing is tight, a call to 660-885-7212 early in the week avoids a rushed visit before a closing.

faqs.q: Who prints the Henry County property tax bill?
faqs.a: The Treasurer, acting as Ex Officio Collector of Revenue, at 100 West Franklin in Clinton. The phone is 660-885-7207.

faqs.q: What percentage applies to a Henry County home?
faqs.a: Nineteen percent of true value. Farmland is assessed at 12 percent and commercial property at 32 percent, and the local levy then applies to the assessed figure.

faqs.q: Is there a grace period after December 31?
faqs.a: Missouri judges mailed payments by postmark, and the collector adds a penalty starting January 1. Ask the collector's office whether any exception applies to you.

faqs.q: Could Henry County sell my home for unpaid tax?
faqs.a: Yes, the statute allows a sale of delinquent land on the fourth Monday of August. Paying the tax, penalty, interest and costs before then stops it.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Henry County assessor?
faqs.a: Call 660-885-7212 or stop by 100 West Franklin in Clinton. Weekday hours are 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and appointments outside those hours are available.
